Tips

  • Name your proficiency precisely on the resume: CEFR level (B2, C1), ACTFL OPI rating, or ILR level.
  • Pair the language with a second skill employers search for: data, writing and editing, business, teaching licensure, or a security clearance path.
  • Many of the best jobs never post to aggregators: check the Search-by-hand list (federal careers, UN and EU, Goethe-Institut, DAAD, American Councils).
  • A semester abroad, an internship, or translation samples count as experience; list them as such.

Search these by hand

  • LinkedIn Jobs — Search 'German speaking' / 'Russian speaking'; export and use --import
  • Indeed — Same searches; also de.indeed.com
  • StepStone (DE) — Largest German private board
  • XING Jobs — German professional network
  • Make it in Germany — Official portal for international applicants
  • Bund.de / Interamt — German federal and state public-sector jobs
  • EURES — EU job mobility portal
  • EU Careers (EPSO) — EU institutions; German is a working language
  • UN Careers — Russian is a UN official language (translators, interpreters, précis-writers)
  • Impactpool — UN agencies, OSCE, development banks
  • OSCE Jobs — Vienna HQ and field missions in Eastern Europe/Central Asia
  • NATO Careers —
  • Devex — International development
  • careers.state.gov — Foreign Service; Russian is a hard-language incentive
  • IntelligenceCareers.gov — NSA, CIA, DIA language analysts
  • FBI Jobs (Language) — Contract linguists and language analysts
  • USAGM / RFE/RL / VOA — Russian- and German-service journalism
  • American Councils — Exchanges and language programs in Eurasia
  • IREX — Education and media development, Eurasia
  • CRDF Global — Science diplomacy, nonproliferation
